test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

When were these pamphlets being distributed?

options.text: When were they distributing these pamphlets?
When are they distributing these pamphlets?
When will they distribute these pamphlets?
When were the distribution of pamphlets happening?

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**.
 
• The structure of the passive voice for past continuous tense is: **was/were + being + past participle.**
 
• To convert this into the active voice, identify the subject performing the action. In this case, the subject is "**they**."
 
• The active voice structure for past continuous tense is: **Subject + was/were + base verb (-ing) + object.**
 
• By applying this structure, the sentence becomes: **"When were they distributing these pamphlets?"**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When were they distributing these pamphlets?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"When are they distributing these pamphlets?" – Incorrect tense (present continuous instead of past continuous).
 
• **Option 3: **"When will they distribute these pamphlets?" – Incorrect tense (future simple instead of past continuous).
 
• **Option 4: **"When were the distribution of pamphlets happening?" – Grammatically incorrect and awkward construction.
